_comment: Pages and the pointer work that reaches them, for tools/parity/capture.py.
Coordinates are WINDOW-RELATIVE: client-area pixels, measured from the top-left
of the page inside the window, at the 1440x900 client area capture.py pins.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS A GUESS. They were written from screenshots of the Modrinth
desktop app on another machine and none of them has been confirmed against this
one. Tune them with both apps up: take one capture, look where the pointer ended,
move the constant it came from, take the capture again. A step that lands on a
control shows up as that control's hover state in a capture that should be idle.
A step is exactly one of: {"move": [x, y]}, {"click": [x, y]},
{"wheel": [x, y, notches]}, {"key": "ctrl+l"}, {"wait": milliseconds}.
Any [x, y] may instead be ["NAME"], one point from `constants` below, so a target
two pages share is written down once and tuned in one place. `wheel` takes the
point plus a notches number: ["NAME", -3] or [720, 400, -3], negative scrolling
down. `key` takes a combination, modifiers first: "ctrl+l", "ctrl+shift+i".
`wait` is milliseconds.
Every page navigates to itself first. A capture has to describe the page, not
whatever page the app happened to be showing when the loop began -- otherwise two
runs of the same command are not comparable and the diff is between two accidents.
States: capture.py adds --state to the filename, so `discover` and `discover-hover`
are two pictures of one page and the second is the pointer resting on a card.
Named client-area points. Some are not used by a page yet: they are the targets
the next pages (library, settings sub-pages) will want, kept here so the tuning
pass has one map to correct instead of four files to correct.
